items.prompt: How do you say "I don't understand"?
items.explanation: Nie goes directly before the verb. There is no helper verb like "do".
optionNotes: Nie goes before the verb, not after it.
One nie before the verb is enough.
Polish has no helper verb: robić means "do, make".

items.explanation: Nikt (nobody) needs nie with the verb: Nikt nie wie.
optionNotes: Nic means "nothing", and the verb still needs nie.
Już means "already"; the verb needs nie.
Też means "too"; the verb needs nie.

items.prompt: You want to know where someone is from. You ask:
optionNotes: Polish does not put the preposition at the end: use skąd.

items.prompt: Czy mówisz po angielsku? — No, I don't.
items.explanation: The first nie means "no", the second makes the verb negative.
optionNotes: This means "No, I do speak": the verb needs its own nie.
Nie goes before the verb, not after it.
